case_studies.title: Operating-Layer Controls for Onchain Language-Model Agents Under Real Capital
case_studies.abstract: We study reliability in autonomous language-model agents that translate user mandates into validated tool actions under real capital. The setting is DX Terminal Pro, a 21-day deployment in which 3,505 user-funded agents traded real ETH in a bounded onchain market. Users configured vaults through structured controls and natural-language strategies, but only agents could choose normal buy/sell trades. The system produced 7.5M agent invocations, roughly 300K onchain actions, about $20M in volume, more than 5,000 ETH deployed, roughly 70B inference tokens, and 99.9% settlement success for policy-v
case_studies.summary: The problem of reliability in autonomous language-model agents is addressed in this study, which explores the use of operating-layer controls to translate user mandates into validated tool actions under real capital. The AI approach involves the deployment of 3,505 user-funded agents in a bounded onchain market, with users configuring vaults through structured controls and natural-language strategies. The outcome is a system that produced 7.5M agent invocations, roughly 300K onchain actions, and a 99.9% settlement success rate for policy validity.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on designing operating-layer controls that allow users to configure and interact with autonomous agents in a secure and reliable manner. By leveraging natural-language strategies and structured controls, practitioners can build more effective and scalable AI systems that can operate in real-world environments.
case_studies.monetisation: The study demonstrates a clear business opportunity for companies to develop and deploy autonomous language-model agents that can operate in onchain markets, with potential applications in areas such as cryptocurrency trading and asset management. By building on the findings of this study, companies can create products and services that provide reliable and secure autonomous trading capabilities, with potential for significant revenue generation.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking Complex Multimodal Document Processing Pipelines: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Enterprise AI
case_studies.abstract: Most enterprise document AI today is a pipeline. Parse, index, retrieve, generate. Each of those stages has been studied to death on its own -- what's still hard is evaluating the system as a whole. We built EnterpriseDocBench to take a swing at it: parsing fidelity, indexing efficiency, retrieval relevance, and generation groundedness, all on the same corpus. The corpus is built from public, permissively licensed documents across six enterprise domains (five represented in the current pilot). We ran three pipelines through it -- BM25, dense embedding, and a hybrid -- all with the same GPT-5 g
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating complex multimodal document processing pipelines is addressed through the introduction of EnterpriseDocBench, a unified evaluation framework. This AI approach involves parsing, indexing, retrieving, and generating documents using three different pipelines: BM25, dense embedding, and a hybrid, all with the same GPT-5 generator. The outcome is a comprehensive evaluation of these pipelines across six enterprise domains, providing insights into their performance and potential areas for improvement.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize the EnterpriseDocBench framework to evaluate their own document processing pipelines, identifying areas for optimization and improvement. By leveraging this framework, practitioners can develop more effective and efficient pipelines, ultimately leading to better document processing outcomes.
case_studies.monetisation: The EnterpriseDocBench framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and sell optimized document processing pipelines to enterprises, leveraging the evaluation framework to demonstrate the value of their solutions. Additionally, the framework can be used to develop new products and services, such as AI-powered document analysis and automation tools, which can be sold to enterprises across various domains.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action models on robots is hindered by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. The AI approach presented in this study involves a systematic analysis of model-hardware co-characterization to evaluate the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators. The outcome of this study shows that right-sized edge devices can be more efficient and effective for low-cost VLA deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this study's findings, AI practitioners should consider evaluating their models on a range of edge devices to find the most efficient and effective combination for their specific use case. By characterizing the constraints and acceleration opportunities of different model-hardware pairs, practitioners can optimize their models for on-robot deployment and improve real-time inference performance.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings have potential business opportunities in the development of more efficient and cost-effective robotic systems, which could be marketed to industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. Companies could leverage the results of this study to create specialized robotic solutions that integrate Vision-Language-Action models with optimized edge devices, providing a competitive advantage in the market.

case_studies.title: HalluCiteChecker: A Lightweight Toolkit for Hallucinated Citation Detection and Verification in the Era of AI Scientists
case_studies.abstract: We introduce HalluCiteChecker, a toolkit for detecting and verifying hallucinated citations in scientific papers. While AI assistant technologies have transformed the academic writing process, including citation recommendation, they have also led to the emergence of hallucinated citations that do not correspond to any existing work. Such citations not only undermine the credibility of scientific papers but also impose an additional burden on reviewers and authors, who must manually verify their validity during the review process. In this study, we formalize hallucinated citation detection as a
case_studies.summary: The emergence of AI-assisted academic writing has led to the problem of hallucinated citations, which undermine the credibility of scientific papers and impose a burden on reviewers and authors. HalluCiteChecker, a lightweight toolkit, approaches this problem by detecting and verifying hallucinated citations using a formalized method. The outcome of this study is a potentially effective solution for improving the accuracy and reliability of scientific citations.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can develop similar toolkits by formalizing the detection of hallucinated information in their respective domains. By leveraging machine learning and natural language processing techniques, practitioners can create effective solutions for verifying the validity of references and citations.
case_studies.monetisation: The HalluCiteChecker toolkit presents a clear product opportunity for companies that provide academic writing and publishing tools, as it can be integrated into existing platforms to enhance the credibility and accuracy of scientific papers. By licensing or developing this technology, companies can offer a unique value proposition to their customers, differentiating themselves in the market and generating revenue through subscription-based models or premium services.

case_studies.title: SynSur: An end-to-end generative pipeline for synthetic industrial surface defect generation and detection
case_studies.abstract: The bottleneck in learning-based industrial defect detection is often limited not by model capacity, but by the scarcity of labeled defect data: defects are rare, annotations are expensive, and collecting balanced training sets is slow. We present an end-to-end pipeline for synthetic defect generation and annotation, combining Vision-Language-Model-based prompts, LoRA-adapted diffusion, mask-guided inpainting, and sample filtering with automatic label derivation, and demonstrates the potential of real data with realistic synthetic samples to overcome data scarcity. The evaluation is conducted
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the scarcity of labeled defect data in industrial defect detection by introducing an end-to-end generative pipeline called SynSur. This pipeline utilizes AI techniques such as Vision-Language-Model-based prompts, LoRA-adapted diffusion, and mask-guided inpainting to generate synthetic defect data. The outcome demonstrates the potential of combining real data with realistic synthetic samples to overcome data scarcity and improve defect detection models.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the SynSur pipeline by integrating it into their existing defect detection workflows, using the generated synthetic data to augment their training sets and improve model performance. To implement this pipeline, practitioners should focus on adapting the AI techniques to their specific use case and ensuring the quality of the generated synthetic data.
case_studies.monetisation: The SynSur pipeline presents a clear business opportunity for companies that specialize in industrial defect detection, as it can help reduce the cost and time associated with data collection and annotation. By developing a product or service based on this pipeline, companies can offer improved defect detection capabilities to their clients, potentially leading to increased revenue and competitiveness.

case_studies.title: Robustness Evaluation of a Foundation Segmentation Model Under Simulated Domain Shifts in Abdominal CT: Implications for Health Digital Twin Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization across natural images; however, their robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. We present a systematic slice-level robustness audit of SAM (ViT-B) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT using 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes in the Medical Segmentation Decathlon. A standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol was used to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty. Controlled perturbations simulatin
case_studies.summary: The robustness of foundation segmentation models under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts is insufficiently quantified, which can impact their deployment in health digital twin applications. To address this, the authors used a systematic slice-level robustness audit of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT scans. The study found that controlled perturbations can simulate domain shifts and evaluate the model's robustness, providing valuable insights for healthcare AI deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by using standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocols to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty in their own models. By doing so, they can systematically evaluate the robustness of their models under various domain shifts, ensuring more reliable performance in real-world applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetized by developing and marketing more robust foundation segmentation models for healthcare applications, such as health digital twin deployment. Companies can leverage these models to create more accurate and reliable medical imaging analysis tools, generating revenue through licensing or subscription-based services.

case_studies.title: Network Impact of Post-Quantum Certificate Chain sizes on Time to First Byte in TLS Deployments
case_studies.abstract: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is a rapidly growing deployment challenge as cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) continue to advance, leaving traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509 vulnerable to attack. However, PQC introduces significant deployment challenges in real-world networks, with handshake sizes increasing from 5x to over 20x compared to classical algorithms. In this work, we evaluate the time to first byte (TTFB) under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of transitioning existing internet infrastructure to quantum-safe certificate s
case_studies.summary: The growing threat of quantum computers compromises traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509, prompting the need for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) deployment. This study evaluates the impact of PQC on Time to First Byte (TTFB) in TLS deployments, focusing on CDN-focused conditions. The outcome characterizes the latency cost of transitioning to quantum-safe certificates, providing insights into the deployment challenges of PQC in real-world networks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the findings of this study, AI practitioners should consider the latency implications of PQC deployment in their own network architectures, and develop strategies to mitigate potential performance degradation. By evaluating the impact of PQC on TTFB, practitioners can optimize their TLS deployments for a seamless transition to quantum-safe cryptography.
case_studies.monetisation: The findings of this study present a clear business opportunity for companies developing quantum-safe cryptographic solutions, as the demand for secure and efficient PQC deployment is expected to grow. By addressing the deployment challenges identified in this study, companies can develop and market optimized PQC solutions, capitalizing on the need for quantum-safe internet infrastructure.

case_studies.title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Static benchmarks measure what AI agents can do at a fixed point in time but not how they are adopted, maintained, or experienced in deployment. We introduce AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework scoring 50 agents across 10 workload categories along four factors (Benchmark Performance, Adoption Signals, Community Sentiment, and Ecosystem Health) aggregated from 18 real-time signals across GitHub, package registries, IDE marketplaces, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards. Three analyses ground the framework. The four factors capture largely complementary information (n=50; $ρ_{\
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating AI agents in deployment is addressed through the introduction of AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework that scores AI agents across multiple factors. The AI approach involves aggregating real-time signals from various sources to provide a comprehensive evaluation of AI agents. The outcome is a framework that captures complementary information, enabling a more holistic understanding of AI agent performance and adoption.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from AgentPulse by incorporating continuous evaluation and multi-signal assessment into their AI development and deployment workflows. This can be achieved by integrating real-time data from various sources, such as GitHub, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards, to gain a more comprehensive understanding of AI agent performance.
case_studies.monetisation: The AgentPulse framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and offer AI evaluation and monitoring services, helping organizations to optimize their AI deployments and improve overall performance. Additionally, the framework's ability to provide actionable insights can be leveraged to create new products or features, such as AI-powered consulting tools or evaluation platforms, that cater to the growing demand for AI solutions.

case_studies.title: MetaSR: Content-Adaptive Metadata Orchestration for Generative Super-Resolution
case_studies.abstract: We study generative super-resolution (SR) in real-world scenarios where content and degradations vary across domains, genres, and segments. For example, images and videos may alternate between text overlays, fast motion, smooth cartoons, and low-light faces, each benefiting from different forms of side information. Existing metadata-guided SR methods typically use a fixed conditioning design, which is suboptimal when useful cues are content dependent and transmission budgets are limited. We propose MetaSR, a Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based framework that selects and injects task-relevant met
case_studies.summary: The problem of generative super-resolution in real-world scenarios is addressed, where content and degradations vary across domains. The proposed AI approach, MetaSR, utilizes a Diffusion Transformer-based framework to select and inject task-relevant metadata. The outcome is a more adaptive and efficient super-resolution method that can handle diverse content types.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can explore the use of metadata-guided approaches in their own super-resolution tasks, considering the content-dependent nature of useful cues. By selecting and injecting relevant metadata, practitioners can improve the efficiency and adaptability of their super-resolution models.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed MetaSR framework has clear product opportunities in the field of computer vision, particularly in applications such as video enhancement and image restoration. Companies can leverage this technology to develop more efficient and adaptive super-resolution products, targeting industries such as media, entertainment, and surveillance.

case_studies.title: Apriori-based Analysis of Learned Helplessness in Mathematics Tutoring: Behavioral Patterns by Level, Intervention, and Outcome
case_studies.abstract: This study applied the Apriori algorithm to analyze behavioral interaction patterns associated with learned helplessness (LH) in mathematics tutoring system logs. Interaction data were examined across three dimensions: LH level (low vs. high), system-based intervention (with vs. without), and problem-solving outcomes (solved vs. unsolved). The analysis of the complete dataset showed that skipping problems without using hints was the most frequent pattern linked to unsolved outcomes, while persistence behaviors such as not skipping were less dominant overall. Comparisons by LH level showed that
case_studies.summary: This study examines the problem of learned helplessness in mathematics tutoring by analyzing interaction patterns in system logs. The Apriori algorithm is used to identify behavioral patterns associated with learned helplessness, system-based intervention, and problem-solving outcomes. The analysis reveals that skipping problems without using hints is linked to unsolved outcomes, while persistence behaviors are less dominant overall.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize the Apriori algorithm to analyze interaction data in various educational settings, providing insights into student behavior and learning outcomes. By identifying patterns associated with learned helplessness, educators and AI developers can design more effective interventions to support students and improve learning outcomes.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this study is the development of AI-powered tutoring systems that incorporate personalized interventions to address learned helplessness, offering a competitive edge in the education technology market. Such a product could be marketed to educational institutions and tutoring services, providing a unique value proposition to improve student outcomes and increase customer engagement.

case_studies.title: Feasible-First Exploration for Constrained ML Deployment Optimization in Crash-Prone Hierarchical Search Spaces
case_studies.abstract: Deploying machine learning models under production constraints requires joint optimization over model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. This induces a hierarchical mixed-variable search space in which many configurations are invalid: evaluations may crash, exceed memory limits, or violate latency constraints. Standard black-box optimizers such as Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE) and constrained Bayesian optimization are effective when valid configurations are common, but they can spend a large fraction of a small evaluation budget on invalid or uni
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying machine learning models under production constraints is addressed through a novel approach that optimizes model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. The proposed AI approach, Feasible-First Exploration, is designed to handle hierarchical mixed-variable search spaces with many invalid configurations. The outcome of this approach is a more efficient optimization of machine learning model deployment, reducing the number of evaluations spent on invalid or uninformative configurations.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners should consider using Feasible-First Exploration to optimize their machine learning model deployment, especially when dealing with complex and constrained search spaces. By doing so, they can reduce the time and resources spent on evaluating invalid configurations and focus on finding the optimal deployment strategy.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed approach has a clear monetisation potential as it can be used to develop more efficient and scalable machine learning model deployment solutions, which can be sold as a product or service to companies looking to optimize their AI workflows. This can be particularly attractive to companies operating in industries with strict production constraints, such as finance or healthcare, where the efficient deployment of machine learning models is crucial.

case_studies.title: Exploring the Potential of Probabilistic Transformer for Time Series Modeling: A Report on the ST-PT Framework
case_studies.abstract: The Probabilistic Transformer (PT) establishes that the Transformer's self-attention plus its feed-forward block is mathematically equivalent to Mean-Field Variational Inference (MFVI) on a Conditional Random Field (CRF). Under this equivalence the Transformer ceases to be a black-box neural network and becomes a programmable factor graph: graph topology, factor potentials, and the message-passing schedule are all explicit and inspectable primitives that can be engineered. PT was originally developed for natural language and in this report we investigate its potential for time series. We first
case_studies.summary: The problem of time series modeling is addressed using the Probabilistic Transformer (PT) framework, which establishes a mathematical equivalence between the Transformer's self-attention and Mean-Field Variational Inference (MFVI) on a Conditional Random Field (CRF). The PT approach allows for a programmable factor graph, enabling explicit and inspectable primitives that can be engineered. The outcome of this investigation is a report on the potential of PT for time series modeling, exploring its applications and implications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the PT framework to time series modeling, practitioners can leverage the equivalence between the Transformer's self-attention and MFVI to design and engineer factor graphs that capture complex temporal relationships. By explicitly defining graph topology, factor potentials, and message-passing schedules, practitioners can create more interpretable and controllable time series models.
case_studies.monetisation: The PT framework has the potential to be monetised through the development of predictive analytics tools for industries that rely heavily on time series data, such as finance and logistics. By creating more accurate and interpretable time series models, companies can provide high-value services to clients, such as demand forecasting and anomaly detection.

case_studies.title: FutureWorld: A Live Environment for Training Predictive Agents with Real-World Outcome Rewards
case_studies.abstract: Live future prediction refers to the task of making predictions about real-world events before they unfold. This task is increasingly studied using large language model-based agent systems, and it is important for building agents that can continually learn from real-world. Just as interactive environments have often driven progress in agents, advancing live future prediction naturally motivates viewing it as a learning environment. Prior works have explored future prediction from several different parts, but have generally not framed it as a unified learning environment. This task is appealing
case_studies.summary: The problem of live future prediction involves making predictions about real-world events before they occur, which is a challenging task that requires advanced agent systems. The proposed AI approach, FutureWorld, frames live future prediction as a unified learning environment, allowing agents to continually learn from real-world outcomes. The outcome of this approach is a more effective and adaptive predictive agent system.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can develop interactive environments that simulate real-world scenarios, allowing agents to learn from outcomes and improve their predictive capabilities. By viewing live future prediction as a learning environment, practitioners can create more effective and adaptive agent systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The FutureWorld approach has potential for monetisation in industries such as finance, healthcare, and logistics, where predictive agents can be used to forecast and prevent adverse events. A concrete business opportunity could involve developing a predictive agent system for a specific industry, using the FutureWorld approach to train and deploy the system.

case_studies.title: Deep-testing: the case of dependence detection
case_studies.abstract: Deep learning methods have proved highly effective for classification and image recognition problems. In this paper, we ask whether this success can be transferred to hypothesis testing: if a neural network can distinguish, for example, an image of a handwritten digit from another, can it also distinguish an "image of a sample" (such as a scatter plot) generated under a given statistical model from one generated outside that model? Motivated by this idea, we propose a novel procedure called deep-testing, which approaches the classical inferential problem of hypothesis testing through deep lear
case_studies.summary: The problem of hypothesis testing in statistical models is addressed through the use of deep learning methods. A novel procedure called deep-testing is proposed, which approaches the classical inferential problem of hypothesis testing through deep learning. The outcome of this approach is a potential new method for distinguishing between samples generated under a given statistical model and those generated outside that model.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this concept by exploring the use of deep learning methods in hypothesis testing, particularly in cases where traditional methods may struggle. By leveraging the capabilities of neural networks, practitioners can develop new procedures for detecting dependencies and making inferences about statistical models.
case_studies.monetisation: The concept of deep-testing has potential for monetisation in fields such as data analytics and statistical consulting, where companies may be willing to pay for advanced methods of hypothesis testing. A potential business opportunity could be to develop a software package or service that implements deep-testing procedures for clients in various industries.

case_studies.title: Calibrated Surprise: An Information-Theoretic Account of Creative Quality
case_studies.abstract: The essence of good creative writing is calibrated surprise: when constraints from all relevant dimensions act together, the feasible solution space collapses into a narrow region, and the surviving choices look least predictable from an unconstrained view. "Calibrated" has a precise meaning: the author's intent, the reader's reasonable expectation, and the logic of reality converge. When these three independent judgements agree on every dimension, the set of admissible writing choices is forced into a very small region. A mathematical corollary follows: full-dimensional accuracy and mediocrit
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating creative writing quality is complex and multifaceted, requiring a nuanced understanding of constraints and predictability. The AI approach proposed in this study uses an information-theoretic account to define calibrated surprise, a key component of creative quality. The outcome is a mathematical framework for understanding how constraints and expectations converge to produce high-quality creative writing.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this concept by incorporating multiple constraints and dimensions into their writing models, allowing for more nuanced and context-dependent generation of text. By using information-theoretic principles to guide the generation of creative content, AI systems can produce more surprising and engaging writing.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of AI-powered writing tools that can help authors and content creators produce more engaging and high-quality writing. Such tools could be marketed to industries such as publishing, advertising, and education, where the ability to generate compelling and effective writing is highly valued.
